title: Generation of human parallel chimeric antigen receptor (pCAR) T cells to achieve synergistic T cell co-stimulation
protocol: Simultaneously digest 2 μg of the pCAR-H/T with NcoI as detailed in Table 1.
Incubate for 60 min at 37°C.
Dephosphorylate the 5′ ends of the linearized plasmid using Quick CIP.
Add 2.5 μL Quick CIP and mix well.
Incubate for an additional 10 min at 37°C.
Heat inactivate the NcoI and Quick CIP simultaneously by incubating at 80°C for 20 min.
Add 10 μL of 6× DNA loading dye to each 50 μL reaction and mix well.
Load each reaction onto a 1% agarose gel containing SYBR Safe.
Also load a 1 kB DNA ladder on the gel.
Run the gel at 100 V until suitable separation between bands is achieved.
Visualize the bands on an UV transilluminator.
Carefully cut around the required bands using a scalpel.
Minimize UV exposure during fragment excision from the agarose gel.
Recover DNA fragments using the Monarch DNA Gel extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute the recovered DNA in 10 μL elution buffer.
Ligate the linearized 2G-A (CD28) or 2G-A (CD28 trunc.) plasmids with the 654 bp TBB_T2A fragment at a 1:3 molar ratio using quick ligase according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

Set up a ligation reaction without the presence of the TBB_T2A band to control for self-ligation of the 2G-A (CD28)/2G-A (CD28 trunc.) backbone and determine the efficiency of the de-phosphorylation step.
Incubate the ligation reaction for 5 minutes at room temperature (approximately 20°C–22°C).
Transform the ligation products into DH5α E.coli cells following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Plate transformed cells onto Petri dishes coated with LB agar containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 16 hours.
Pick individual colonies in a 14 mL Falcon polypropylene tube with a loose snap cap.
Grow the colonies in 3 mL Luria Broth containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin for 16 hours at 37°C with agitation at 180 rpm.
Isolate plasmid DNA from E. coli using the Monarch Plasmid Miniprep Kit, following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Perform a diagnostic restriction digest to confirm the successful insertion of the TBB_T2A fragment.
Seed HEK293T cells.
Transfect HEK293T cells using GeneJuice® Transfection Reagent.
(Optional) Replace medium if a toxic transfection reagent was used.
Aspirate 48 h viral supernatant and store at 4°C for 18 hours.
Replenish the medium after aspirating the 48 h viral supernatant.
Aspirate 72 h viral supernatant and pool with the 48 h harvest.
Prepare 1.5 mL aliquots of the pooled viral supernatant.
Snap freeze the prepared aliquots.
Store the frozen aliquots at -80°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of pre-warmed D10 medium.
Transfer the suspension to a 75 cm³ culture flask.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Rinse the 75 cm³ flask with 5 mL PBS to remove residual serum if needed.
Discard the PBS after rinsing.
Add 3 mL of Trypsin-EDTA solution to the flask.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 5–15 minutes.
Confirm that the cell layer has detached under an inverted microscope.
Add 7 mL D10 medium to inactivate trypsin.
Split cells to a 1:10 ratio by adding 1 mL of trypsinized cells to 9 mL fresh D10 in a new flask.
Seed HEK293T cells into 10 cm² tissue culture dishes one day prior to transfection.
Add 3 mL of Trypsin-EDTA solution.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 5–15 min.
Confirm cell detachment by observing under an inverted microscope.
Add 5 mL of I10 medium to the cells.
Count the cells using trypan blue and a hemocytometer.
Re-suspend cells to a final concentration of 1.5 × 10^5/mL in I10 medium.
Add 11 mL of cell suspension to each 10 cm² culture dish (1.65 × 10^6 cells per dish).
Gently rock the dishes from side to side for even distribution.
Place dishes in an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Mix 470 μL serum-free IMDM medium with 30 μL GeneJuice® in a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Pipette up and down and incubate at room temperature (approximately 20°C–22°C) for 5 min.
Add 4.6875 μg PeqPam3 plasmid to the mixture.
Add 3.125 μg RDF plasmid to the mixture.
Add 4.6875 μg of the appropriate retroviral vector plasmid to the mixture.
Mix gently using pipette and incubate for 15 min at room temperature (approximately 20°C–22°C).
Add total volume dropwise to the HEK293T plate.
Swirl contents thoroughly in the plate.
Incubate cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 48 hours.
Change medium on HEK293T cells 24 hours after transfection by adding 11 mL of fresh I10 medium pre-warmed to 37°C.
Label a 50 mL Falcon tube for each transfected dish of HEK293T cells.
Place Falcon tubes on ice for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant from HEK293T cells and place into the pre-chilled 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Replenish 11 mL of I10 medium (pre-warmed to 37°C) to each dish and return to the incubator.
Store the Falcon tubes containing 48-hour supernatant in a 4°C refrigerator for 24 hours.
Prepare an ethanol bath by adding 100% ethanol into a rubber container until the tube rack is submerged.
Add dry ice to the bath until level with the ethanol.
Remove 72-hour supernatant from HEK293T cells and combine with 48-hour supernatant on ice.
Filter the combined supernatant using a 0.45 μm sterile filter (optional).
Prepare 1.5 mL aliquots of supernatant into labeled tubes.
Put the aliquoted supernatants into the ethanol bath rack until completely frozen.
Transfer tubes to -80°C storage as soon as possible once frozen.
Pool blood from 9 mL vacuette tubes into 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Wash each vacuette tube with 5 mL sterile PBS and add to the pooled blood.
Aliquot 15 mL Ficoll-Paque PLUS into 50 mL Falcon tubes (1 Falcon tube per 35 mL whole blood).
Layer 30 mL of PBS-diluted whole blood on top of the Ficoll-Paque Plus in each Falcon tube using a pipette aid and a 25 mL stripette.
Centrifuge all tubes at 800 × g for 35 min with brake and acceleration both set to zero.
Carefully remove the PBMC layer from the Falcon tubes using a Pasteur pipette and transfer into a fresh 50 mL Falcon tube.
Take care not to draw up Ficoll-Paque PLUS when removing the PBMC layer.
Add sterile PBS to a final volume of 50 mL per Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at room temperature (approximately 20°C–22°C).
Remove supernatant, being careful not to disturb the cell pellet.
Add 1 mL PBS to each pellet, re-suspend, and combine in a single fresh 50 mL Falcon tube.
Wash all tubes with 5 mL sterile PBS and combine with previously harvested PBMCs.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at room temperature (approximately 20°C–22°C).
Aspirate PBS, being careful not to disturb the cell pellet.
Re-suspend cell pellet in 10 mL R5 medium (RPMI + 2 mM L-glutamine + 5% human male AB serum).
Mix 10 μL PBMC suspension with 10 μL trypan blue and count using a hemocytometer.
Dilute PBMCs using R5 medium to achieve a final concentration of 3 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Seed cells into tissue culture-treated 6 well plates containing 4 mL per well.
Add phytohemagglutinin (PHA)-L to T cells to a final concentration of 5 μg/mL and mix well.
Incubate at 37°C & 5% CO2 for 48 h.
Do not add or change medium over this period.
After 24 hours, add 100 IU/mL recombinant human IL-2 to activated PBMCs.
Optional: Prior to activation, isolate T cells from the PBMC population according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Coat RetroNectin® on non-tissue culture (TC) treated 6 well plates.
Pre-load the coated plates with viral supernatant.
Add viral supernatant, IL-2 and activated T cells to the pre-loaded plates.
Incubate for 72 hours at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Add 200 μL RetroNectin® (1 mg/mL stock solution) to 18 mL sterile PBS in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Aliquot 3 mL of the mixture into each well of a non-tissue culture-treated 6 well plate.
Wrap the 6 well plate in Saran Wrap and store for 18 h at 4°C.
Rapidly thaw 1.5 mL aliquots of viral supernatant in a 37°C water bath for the constructs of choice.
Spray cryovials containing viral supernatant with 70% ethanol and transfer into a laminar flow hood.
Pre-load the RetroNectin®-coated 6 well plate with viral vector by removing RetroNectin® from each individual well.
Promptly add 1.5 mL of thawed viral supernatant to avoid drying.
Incubate the virus-coated six well plate for 2 h at approximately 20°C–22°C or overnight at 4°C.
Retrieve activated T cells from the 6 well plate and transfer them into a Falcon tube.
Gently mix by inversion and count using a hemocytometer and Trypan blue.
Aspirate the 1.5 mL viral vector from the preloaded RetroNectin®-coated 6 well plate.
Add 3 mL of freshly thawed viral supernatant to each well for transduction.
For non-transduced control T cells, add 3 mL D10 medium (DMEM + 2 mM L-glutamine + 10% fetal bovine serum).
Add 1 × 10^6 activated T cells per well of the 6 well plate directly from the activated PBMC culture.
Do not adjust the concentration of the activated T cells.
Add IL-2 to each well to a final concentration of 100 IU/mL.
Incubate cells at 37°C and 5% CO₂ for 72 h.
Do not wash activated T cells prior to transduction as this will remove stimulatory factors present in the medium.
Supplement T cells with medium and IL-2 every 2–3 days to expand in culture.
Quantify cell surface expression of CAR and pCAR by flow cytometry using appropriate antibodies.
Feed T cells with 100% volume increase of R5 medium every 2 days (3 days if over weekends).
Add recombinant human IL-2 to a final concentration of 100 IU/mL when feeding the T cells.
Maintain T cell concentration below 1 × 10^6 cells/ml.
If T cell density is below 5 × 10^5/ml, add only 100 IU/ml recombinant human IL-2.
Transfer 2.5 × 10^5 T cells for each CAR construct into separate 5 mL flow cytometry tubes.
Prepare two separate tubes containing 2.5 × 10^5 non-transduced T cells.
Wash each tube with 2 mL PBS and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Discard PBS and resuspend the cell pellet in 50 μL PBS.
Add 25 μL anti-human MYC (9e10) hybridoma supernatant to all tubes containing transduced T cells and one non-transduced tube.
Place on ice for 30 min.
Wash each tube with 2 mL PBS and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Discard PBS and add fresh 50 μL PBS to each tube.
Add 3 μL goat anti-mouse IgG PE conjugated antibody to each tube.
Place on ice for 30 min in the dark.
Wash each tube with 2 mL PBS and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Discard PBS and add fresh 50 μL PBS to each tube.
Add 10 μL mouse serum (diluted 1:10 in PBS) to each tube.
Incubate at room temperature (approximately 20°C–22°C) for 30 min in the dark.
Mix 3 μL biotinylated anti-human EGF with each tube.
Place tubes on ice for 30 min in the dark.
Wash each tube with 2 mL PBS.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Discard PBS from each tube.
Add fresh 50 μL PBS to each tube.
Mix 3 μL SA-APC with each tube.
Incubate on ice for 30 min in the dark.
Wash each tube with 2 mL PBS.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min and return tubes to ice.
Discard PBS from each tube.
Resuspend cells in 250 μL PBS.
Analyze using flow cytometry.
Seed tumor cells in three replicate 24 well plates for analysis at 24, 48, and 72 hours after adding pCAR T cells.
Add 1 × 10^5 pCAR or control T cells to triplicate wells of tumor cells according to the indicated matrix after 24 hours.
Harvest supernatant at each time point for ELISA measurement of IL-2 and IFN-γ.
Perform MTT assay at each time point to determine residual tumor cell viability.
Seed tumor cells at 1 × 10^5 cells in 500 μL D10 medium per well in tissue culture treated 24-well plates.
Incubate the seeded tumor cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Count CAR and pCAR T cells.
Re-suspend each type of transduced T cells to a final concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells/mL in R5 medium.
Aspirate the medium from the tumor cells without disturbing the monolayers.
Add 1 mL of CAR, pCAR or non-transduced T cells per well of tumor cells in triplicate.
Add 1 mL of R5 medium to three wells as tumor alone control.
Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Transfer 150 μL supernatant from each well into a labeled u-bottom 96-well plate.
Store the transferred supernatants at -20°C for cytokine analysis.
Reconstitute MTT at a concentration of 5 mg/mL in PBS.
Dilute MTT stock solution 1:10 in R10 medium to achieve a final concentration of 500 μg/mL.
Remove remaining medium from each well of one 24-well plate, leaving two plates for analysis after 48 h and 72 h.
Pipette 500 μL of the 500 μg/mL MTT solution into each well.
Incubate at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Aspirate MTT solution from each well without disturbing the monolayers.
Add 500 μL DMSO to each well.
Gently swirl the plate to solubilize formazan crystals.
Read absorbance at 560 nm using a plate reader.
Calculate residual tumor cell viability as (Absorbance of tumor + T cells / Absorbance of tumor + medium control) × 100.
Analyze cytokine production on day 3, 4, and 5.
Assess the concentration of IL-2 in harvested supernatants using ELISA by diluting supernatants 1:5 in reagent diluent.
Assess the concentration of IFNγ in harvested supernatants using ELISA by diluting supernatants 1:10 in reagent diluent.
Seed tumor cells on day 1.
On day 2, add 1 × 10^5 pCAR or control T cells to tumor cells.
On day 4, seed tumor cells for stimulation cycle 2.
Optional: On days 3, 4, and/or 5, collect supernatant from stimulation cycle 1 for ELISA.
Perform MTT assay on day 5 to determine tumor cell viability (stimulation cycle 1).
Retrieve and pool pCAR and control T cells from stimulation 1 well plate.
Plate retrieved pCAR and control T cells on tumor cells in stimulation cycle 2 plate.
Repeat steps 3–7 until T cells can no longer be retrieved from tumor monolayers.
Re-stimulate pCAR-A/T and control T cells on the indicated tumor cell lines.
Validate tumor cell surface expression of the target antigen(s) recognized by the CAR or pCAR under study prior to co-culture experiments.
Seed tumor cells at 1 × 10^5 cells in D10 medium per well in a tissue culture treated 24 well plate, with a total volume of 500 μL per well.
Incubate the seeded plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Count CAR and pCAR T cells.
Re-suspend each CAR and pCAR T cell type to a final concentration of 1 × 10^5 transduced T cells/mL in R5 medium.
Prepare untransduced T cells at an equivalent density per mL as the highest density of total T cells present in the CAR and pCAR T cell tubes.
Aspirate the medium from the tumor cells, being careful not to disturb the monolayers.
Add 1 mL of CAR, pCAR or non-transduced T cells per well of tumor cells in triplicate.
Add 1 mL of R5 medium to three wells as a tumor alone control.
Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Harvest 150 μL supernatant from each well for cytokine analysis by ELISA, transferring into a labeled u-bottom 96 well plate and storing at −20°C (optional).
Seed tumor cells at 1 × 10^5 cells per well in a tissue culture treated 24 well plate with a total volume of 500 μL per well for stimulation cycle 2.
Incubate the seeded plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Analyze stimulation cycle 1.
Transfer 150 μL supernatant from each co-cultivation well into a labeled u-bottom 96 well plate and store at −20°C (optional).
Prepare MTT to a concentration of 500 μg/mL (13 mL/24 well plate).
Carefully remove the medium from each well of one 24 well plate.
Pool triplicate wells into single 15 mL Falcon tubes.
Wash wells with 1 mL PBS.
Transfer washed contents to corresponding 15 mL Falcon tubes.
Pipette 500 μL of 500 μg/mL MTT solution into each well.
Incubate 24-well plate at 37°C and 5% CO₂ for 1 hour.
Centrifuge 15 mL Falcon tubes containing T cells at 400 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate supernatant carefully to avoid disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 3.2 mL R5 medium.
Aspirate medium from tumor cells seeded on day 4.
Add 1 mL of T cells to corresponding wells.
Incubate plate at 37°C and 5% CO₂ (stimulation 2).
With remaining 200 μL cell suspension, count using trypan blue.
Aspirate MTT solution from each well carefully not to disturb monolayers.
Add 500 μL DMSO into each well.
Gently swirl the plate to solubilize formazan crystals.
Read absorbance at 560 nm using a plate reader.
Calculate residual tumor cell viability using the formula (Absorbance of tumor + T cells/Absorbance of tumor + medium control) × 100.
Repeat steps for preparing tumor cells on day 1, day 5, day 8, day 12 and T cells on day 2, day 6, day 9, day 13 until T cells can no longer be retrieved at the end of a stimulation cycle.
Tumor injection into NSG mice.
Perform bioluminescence imaging to confirm tumor engraftment and distribute mice into treatment groups with similar mean tumor burden.
Inject pCAR, CAR, and control T cells or PBS.
Monitor tumor status by serial BLI.
Evaluate anti-tumor activity of pCAR-A/T and control T cells in NSG mice with an established BxPC3 tumor burden.
Administer T cell treatments 12 days after tumor cell inoculation.
Monitor tumor burden in individual mice by BLI.
Create Kaplan Meier survival curves.
Measure weight of treated mice (mean ± SEM).
Take baseline weight readings on the day of tumor injection.
Check mice for signs of ill health before tumor injection.
Inject 1 × 10^5 ffLuc/RFP-expressing BxPC3 tumor cells suspended in 100 μL sterile PBS into all mice using the i.p. route.
Weigh mice twice weekly and check for signs of ill health.
Sacrifice mice if weight loss exceeds 15% due to tumor burden.
Humanely kill mice if tumor total flux reading equals or exceeds 1 × 10¹⁰, or if the tumor ulcerates, limits normal behavior, impedes a vital function, or causes clinical signs such as jaundice.

Consider an increase in body girth similar to a pregnant mouse, dyspnea, neurological signs, lameness, and general signs of ill-health (e.g., piloerection, hunched posture, inability to groom, inactivity, inappetance) as humane endpoints.
Inject mice intraperitoneally with 150 mg/kg D-luciferin on Day 6.
Place mice into an anesthetic induction chamber until fully anesthetized (isoflurane 2.5%, flow rate 2L/min).
Image the mice using the IVIS Spectrum Imaging platform and Living Image software precisely 15 minutes after the D-luciferin injection.
Determine the D-luciferin kinetic curve for your model following Perkin Elmer protocols.
Create a region of interest over each entire mouse to determine total flux (photons/second).
Return mice to their cages after imaging until they fully regain consciousness.
Perform serial imaging every 5 min until 40 min post substrate injection.
Plot total flux against time to determine the optimal imaging time point for maximum total flux.
Distribute mice into treatment groups with similar average tumor burden if total flux values are greater than the enrollment threshold.
Administer T cells and PBS.
Count transduced and non-transduced T cells.
Prepare transduced T cells in PBS at a concentration of 2 × 10^7 transduced T cells/mL.
Weigh mice.
Inject 200 μL of either pCAR, CAR or non-transduced T cells i.p. into the mice.
Inject 200 μL PBS into control mice.
Monitor mice daily for signs of ill health.
Weigh mice twice weekly.
Perform weekly bioluminescence imaging (BLI) for tumor status monitoring throughout the study.
Clone alternative TNFr domains into SFG plasmid vector encoding pCAR-A/T.
Synthesize DNA fragments as codon optimized sequences inserted in the pUCIDT plasmid (IDT).

Encode amino acids 137–206 of CD8α, fused in frame with either amino acids 213–260 of CD27, amino acids 408–595 of CD30, amino acids 216–277 of CD40, amino acids 221–417 of DR3, amino acids 184–241 of Glucocortocoid-induced TNFR-related protein (GITR), or amino acids 224–283 of Herpes virus entry mediator (HVEM).
Include a furin cleavage site (RRKR) in the fragments.
Add an [SG]2 linker to the fragments.
Insert a T2A ribosomal skip peptide into the fragments.
Encode the IL-4 receptor signal peptide in the fragments.
Incorporate the A20FMDV peptide (Whilding et al., 2017).
Include an [A]3 linker in the fragments.
Add amino acids 114–134 of CD28 to the fragments, replacing amino acids 117–122 with the myc tag sequence.
Amplify fragments by PCR using primers BD_008 and BD_006.
Fuse amplified products by overlap extension PCR with a secondary fragment generated from pCAR-A/T using primers PR_031 and BD_007.
Clone the resulting PCR products into pCAR-A/T as an NcoI-NotI fragment.
Isolate T cells.
Activate isolated T cells.
Transduce activated T cells.
Expand transduced T cells.
Analyze T cells for pCAR expression.
Perform tumor re-stimulation assays on BxPC3 tumor cells.
